title: How a session is obtained and how the API decides who is calling
summary: Google sign-in and the loopback-only developer shortcut, then the three token paths the gate tries and the authorisation rule that differs by mode.
note: Two things here are gated closed in a default build. The developer shortcut is off unless AUTH_ENABLE_DEV_LOGIN is set — .env.example:56 sets it true for local work — and packages/config/src/env.ts:117 refuses to start a NODE_ENV=production process with it set at all; even when on it answers only loopback callers. Cloud enrolment is off unless VITAE_CLOUD_ENABLED is set, which .env.example:40 leaves false, so in a default build /auth/bootstrap returns 409 SELF_HOSTED_MODE and the OWNER_EMAIL comparison is the whole authorisation rule. GET /auth/me is the one route in this flow reachable without a session; it is special-cased above the public-path check rather than by it.

actors.label: Browser (AuthProvider)
actors.note: Renders only what /auth/me returns; it never chooses a workspace or decides that Cloud is on.

actors.label: Firebase / Google
actors.note: Issues the ID token. In dev builds this is the Auth emulator, whose first onAuthStateChanged can lag by seconds.

actors.label: /api/v1/auth/*
actors.note: dev-login, logout and me are public paths; bootstrap deliberately is not.

actors.label: authGate
actors.note: Mounted at /api (app.ts:62). Resolves a token, then applies a mode-dependent authorisation rule.

actors.label: Control plane
actors.note: Owns identities, memberships and lifecycle. Reached only after the gate has proved an identity.

steps.label: GET /auth/me on load, before anything is signed in
steps.note: Public because the browser has to ask who it is before it can render a sign-in screen. It returns nulls plus two deployment booleans: cloudEnabled and devLoginEnabled.

steps.label: /auth/me is matched before the public-path check and resolves a token if one is present
steps.note: A special case at auth.ts:128, not the PUBLIC_PATHS list. It sets req.user opportunistically and always calls next(), so the route answers signed-out without a 401.

steps.label: signInWithGoogle popup
steps.note: Only offered when the build carries Firebase config (googleSignInAvailable). The ID token is then read per request by setAuthTokenProvider(currentIdToken).

steps.label: POST /auth/dev-login (local development only)
steps.note: The browser offers this button only under Vite DEV on a loopback hostname (apps/web/src/lib/runtime.ts:13). That is a UI courtesy; the server checks independently.

steps.label: 403 DEV_LOGIN_DISABLED or 403 DEV_LOGIN_REMOTE
steps.note: Defence in depth, three independent conditions: the flag must be set, the socket's remote address must be loopback, and the env schema refuses to boot production with the flag on at all.

steps.label: Set-Cookie vitae_session (httpOnly, sameSite lax, 24h)
steps.note: The token is the session and is not echoed in the body — that would put an owner credential in JS reach and in every proxy log. The one exception is an emulator run, where the test client has no cookie jar.

steps.label: any /api call: Authorization: Bearer <token>, else the session cookie
steps.note: The client prefers a bearer token when a provider supplies one and otherwise relies on credentials: 'include'. The gate reads them in the same order.

steps.label: path 1: verify as a local dev JWT (SESSION_SECRET, no network)
steps.note: Tried first because it is free. Accepted only when the payload carries via === 'dev'.

steps.label: path 2: verifyIdToken against the primary Firebase project
steps.note: Accepted only when email_verified is true AND the sign-in provider is google.com. Anything else falls through as if invalid.

steps.label: path 3: verifyIdToken against the configured companion project
steps.note: Only when trustedAuth is configured. Held to the same strict bar, and its uid is prefixed 'trusted:' so a coincidental collision can never alias a primary Cloud account.

steps.label: 401 UNAUTHORIZED — neutral, identical for every rejection reason
steps.note: Self-host: the verified email must equal OWNER_EMAIL. Cloud: any verified google or dev identity with a uid passes here, and membership decides the rest. The message never reveals the allow-list.

steps.label: identity proved; Cloud resolves a workspace for this uid
steps.note: Skipped when cloudEnabled() is false, and skipped for /auth/bootstrap, /auth/me and /auth/logout, which must work before a workspace exists.

steps.label: POST /auth/bootstrap when Cloud is on and /auth/me returned no workspace
steps.note: Idempotent, so a restored Google session and a fresh sign-in behave identically. Not public: it creates a private workspace and starts a trial.

steps.label: upsert the user, create one personal workspace, start the trial
steps.note: A verified email already bound to a different uid raises IdentityConflictError → 409, rather than silently attaching one person's identity to another's records.

steps.label: { user, workspace, self, cloudEnabled, devLoginEnabled }
steps.note: /auth/me swallows a graph or database failure and returns self as null: the owner check already passed, and auth must not fail while the graph is degraded.
